levels.name: Premiers pas
levels.desc: Découvrir les sons de l’anglais, l’alphabet et tes tout premiers mots.

units.title: Les sons de l’anglais
units.goal: Reconnaître et prononcer les lettres et les sons propres à l’anglais.

content.title: L’alphabet
content.objective: Reconnaître et prononcer les 26 lettres en anglais.

explanation.text: L’anglais utilise les mêmes 26 lettres que le français, mais leurs noms se prononcent autrement. Touche chaque lettre du tableau pour l’entendre.
Le grand piège : A se dit « é-i », E se dit « i » et I se dit « aï ». C’est presque l’inverse du français!
G se dit « dji » et J se dit « djé-i ». On les mélange souvent : pense à « Gee! » et au prénom « Jay ».
Z se dit « zed » au Canada et en Angleterre, et « zi » aux États-Unis. Les deux sont corrects.

examples.fr: La radio-télévision publique anglophone du Canada : « si-bi-si ».

vocab.example: A bee is on the flower.

tip.text: Plusieurs lettres sonnent comme des mots : B = bee, C = see, I = eye, U = you, Y = why. C’est pour ça qu’on écrit « C U » pour « see you » dans les textos!

exercises.explain: J se dit « djé-i » (comme Jay). G se dit « dji ».
E se dit « i » en anglais.
I se dit « aï », comme le mot eye (œil).

exercises.question: The letter ___ sounds like the word « why ».
exercises.explain: Y se dit « ouaï », comme why (pourquoi).

exercises.question: In Canada, the letter Z is usually called « ___ ».
exercises.explain: Au Canada, on dit « zed ». Aux États-Unis, « zee ».

content.title: Épeler en anglais
content.objective: Épeler ton nom, ton courriel et comprendre un mot épelé.

explanation.text: Au téléphone, au bureau ou à la frontière, on te demandera souvent : « Can you spell that, please? » (Pouvez-vous épeler?).
Pour une lettre double, on dit « double » : Anne = A, double N, E. Pour une majuscule : « capital A ».
Dans un courriel : @ se dit « at », le point « dot », le tiret « dash » et _ « underscore ».
Pour éviter les confusions (B/P, M/N), on précise : « B as in Boy », « N as in Nancy ».

examples.en: Can you spell your last name, please?
examples.fr: Pouvez-vous épeler votre nom de famille?

examples.en: My email is marie dot roy at gmail dot com.
Is that B as in Boy?
Pelletier: P, E, double L, E, T, I, E, R.
examples.fr: Pelletier : P, E, deux L, E, T, I, E, R.

vocab.example: How do you spell your name?

dialogue.en: Can you spell your last name?
dialogue.fr: Pouvez-vous épeler votre nom de famille?

dialogue.en: Sure. T, R, E, M, B, L, A, Y.
dialogue.fr: Bien sûr. T, R, E, M, B, L, A, Y.

dialogue.en: Thank you. And your email address?
It’s marie dot tremblay at gmail dot com.

tip.text: Les francophones confondent souvent E et I en épelant. Entraîne-toi avec ton propre nom : c’est le mot que tu épelleras le plus souvent!

exercises.explain: T, O, M : Tom. O se dit « ô-ou ».
E se dit « i » : E, V, A = Eva.
J (« djé-i »), A (« é-i »), C, K : Jack.

exercises.question: In an email address, « @ » is read ___.

exercises.explain: La question commence par Can : Can you spell…?

exercises.question: How do you say « deux L » when you spell a name?

lessons.title: Les sons TH, H, R et W

content.title: Les sons TH, H, R et W
content.objective: Prononcer les sons anglais qui n’existent pas en français.

explanation.text: TH : place le bout de la langue entre tes dents et souffle. Doux dans « think » (penser), vibrant dans « this » (ceci). Évite « tink » ou « dis »!
H : en anglais, le H se prononce! Souffle comme sur une vitre : « hello », « happy », « house ». Attention : « eat » (manger) ≠ « heat » (chaleur).
R : la langue recule sans toucher le palais et les lèvres s’arrondissent un peu. Pas de R roulé ni de R de gorge : « red », « car ».
W : arrondis les lèvres comme pour « ou » : « water », « what », « window ». C’est le « ou » de « oui ».

examples.en: I think this is the third one.
examples.fr: Je pense que c’est le troisième.

examples.en: The red car is really fast.

tip.text: Paires à pratiquer avec 🔊 : three / tree (trois / arbre), hair / air (cheveux / air), eat / heat (manger / chaleur), think / sink (penser / évier).

exercises.explain: « three » commence par TH : la langue entre les dents.
On entend le souffle du H : hair (cheveux).

exercises.question: Which word starts with a TH sound?
exercises.explain: think : la langue entre les dents.
W : lèvres arrondies comme « ou » : west (ouest).
Thank you for + nom : Thank you for the help.

content.title: Voyelles courtes et longues
content.objective: Entendre la différence entre les voyelles courtes et longues (ship / sheep).

explanation.text: « sheep » (mouton) a un i long : étire-le en souriant. « ship » (bateau) a un i court et détendu, entre « i » et « é ».
« full » (plein) a un « ou » court, « fool » (idiot) un « ou » long. Même chose pour « pull » et « pool ».
Une voyelle mal prononcée change le sens : « leave » (partir) ≠ « live » (vivre).
Truc : une voyelle longue s’étire, une voyelle courte est rapide et relâchée. Compare les paires avec 🔊.

vocab.example: The ship is in the port.

tip.text: Le « i » court anglais n’existe pas en français. Pense à un « i » paresseux, presque un « é » : sit, big, fish, it.

exercises.question: Which word has a LONG vowel?

exercises.sentence: I live in a big city
exercises.explain: Sujet + verbe + lieu : I live in…

units.title: Mes premiers mots
units.goal: Saluer, compter, décrire les couleurs et parler du calendrier.

content.title: Bonjour et politesse
content.objective: Saluer, remercier, t’excuser et dire au revoir poliment.

explanation.text: Pour saluer : « Hi! » (familier), « Hello! » (neutre), « Good morning / Good afternoon / Good evening » (plus poli).
Les mots magiques : please (s’il te plaît), thank you ou thanks (merci), you’re welcome (de rien).
« Sorry! » si tu bouscules quelqu’un, « Excuse me » pour attirer l’attention ou pour passer.
Pour partir : « Bye! », « See you! », « Have a nice day! ». « Good night » veut dire bonne nuit, jamais bonsoir.

examples.fr: Je vais bien, merci. Et toi?

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the washroom?

vocab.example: Excuse me, is this seat free?

dialogue.en: Hi! I’m Sam. Nice to meet you.
Hi Sam! I’m Julie. Nice to meet you too.
dialogue.fr: Salut Sam! Moi, c’est Julie. Enchantée aussi.

tip.text: « How are you? » est souvent une simple salutation. On répond brièvement (« Good, thanks! And you? ») sans raconter sa journée.

exercises.question: Someone says « Thank you! ». You answer: « ___ »
You arrive at a party at 8 p.m. You say: « Good ___! »
exercises.explain: Good evening = bonsoir. Good night = bonne nuit (en partant ou au coucher).
Nice to meet you = enchanté (première rencontre).

exercises.sentence: Excuse me, where is the washroom?

exercises.question: You bump into someone. You say: « ___ »

exercises.explain: Have a nice day : une formule très courante.

content.title: Les nombres de 0 à 20
content.objective: Compter de 0 à 20 et donner ton numéro de téléphone.

explanation.text: 0 zero, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five, 6 six, 7 seven, 8 eight, 9 nine, 10 ten.
11 eleven, 12 twelve, puis on ajoute « -teen » : thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen. 20 = twenty.
Pour un numéro de téléphone, on dit chaque chiffre : 514-555-0198 = five one four, five five five, oh one nine eight. Le 0 se dit souvent « oh ».
« three » commence par TH (≠ tree, arbre) et « eight » rime avec « day ».

examples.en: My number is five one four, five five five, oh one nine eight.
I have two cats and one dog.
examples.fr: J’ai deux chats et un chien.
Le magasin ouvre à huit heures.

tip.text: De 13 à 19, l’accent tombe sur « teen » : thirTEEN, fifTEEN. Ça évite de confondre avec thirty, fifty (prochaine leçon).

exercises.audio: five one four, two oh three
exercises.explain: Chiffre par chiffre, et « oh » pour 0.

exercises.sentence: My phone number is five one four
exercises.fr: Mon numéro de téléphone est cinq un quatre

content.title: Les nombres jusqu’à 100
content.objective: Compter jusqu’à 100, dire ton âge et des prix simples.

explanation.text: Les dizaines : 20 twenty, 30 thirty, 40 forty (sans « u »!), 50 fifty, 60 sixty, 70 seventy, 80 eighty, 90 ninety, 100 one hundred.
On ajoute l’unité avec un trait d’union : 21 twenty-one, 45 forty-five, 99 ninety-nine. Pas de « soixante-dix » ni de « quatre-vingts » : c’est plus simple qu’en français!
Piège : thirTEEN (13) a l’accent à la fin, THIRty (30) au début. Compare avec 🔊.
Pour l’âge, on utilise « be » : I’m 34 (years old). Jamais « I have 34 ».

examples.en: I live at forty-four Maple Street.

tip.text: Au Canada, on dit les prix ainsi : 3,50 $ = « three fifty », 12,99 $ = « twelve ninety-nine ».

exercises.question: 40 is written ___.
exercises.explain: forty, sans « u », même si four en a un.

exercises.question: « J’ai 25 ans » = « ___ twenty-five. »
exercises.explain: L’âge se dit avec be : I’m twenty-five.

content.title: Les couleurs
content.objective: Nommer les couleurs et décrire des objets du quotidien.

explanation.text: red (rouge), blue (bleu), green (vert), yellow (jaune), black (noir), white (blanc), orange, pink (rose), purple (mauve), brown (brun), gray (gris).
En anglais, la couleur vient AVANT le nom : a blue car (une auto bleue), a red apple (une pomme rouge).
Les adjectifs ne prennent jamais de « s » : two black cats, jamais « blacks ».
Pour nuancer : light blue (bleu pâle), dark green (vert foncé). Pour demander : « What color is it? »

examples.fr: Ma couleur préférée est le vert.

examples.en: What color is a banana? It’s yellow.
examples.fr: De quelle couleur est une banane? Jaune.

tip.text: « Purple » = mauve ou violet, et « brown » = brun. Au Canada, on écrit aussi « colour » et « grey » (orthographe britannique).

exercises.question: « Une pomme rouge » = « ___ »
exercises.explain: La couleur se place avant le nom.

exercises.fr: Ma couleur préférée est le vert

content.title: Les jours et les mois
content.objective: Dire les jours, les mois et la date.

explanation.text: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Ils prennent toujours une majuscule!
January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December. Majuscule aussi.
On dit « on » pour un jour ou une date (on Monday, on May 5th) et « in » pour un mois ou une année (in May, in 2025).
Pour la date, on utilise first, second, third, fourth… : « My birthday is on June 24th » (twenty-fourth).

examples.en: It snows a lot in December.
I work from Monday to Friday.
examples.fr: Je travaille du lundi au vendredi.

tip.text: Wednesday se prononce « WENZ-day » : le premier « d » est muet!

levels.name: Débutant
levels.desc: Te présenter, parler de ton quotidien et comprendre des phrases simples.

units.title: Se présenter
units.goal: Dire qui tu es, d’où tu viens et poser des questions simples.

lessons.title: « Je suis… » : le verbe to be
lessons.brief: Verb to be in the present: affirmative full and contracted forms (I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're) and subject pronouns. Introducing yourself: name, age, job, feelings. Pitfall for French speakers: age uses be, not have (I am 30, never I have 30).

lessons.title: Questions et négations avec to be
lessons.brief: Negative forms of be (I'm not, isn't, aren't) and yes/no questions (Are you…? Is she…?) with short answers (Yes, I am / No, he isn't). Question words: what, where, who, how old, how are you.

lessons.title: Pays, nationalités et langues
lessons.brief: Countries, nationalities and languages (Canada/Canadian, France/French, the United States/American, Mexico/Mexican, China/Chinese, Haiti/Haitian…). Capital letters for nationalities and languages in English. Where are you from? I'm from Quebec. I speak French and a little English.

lessons.title: My, your, his, her : les possessifs
lessons.brief: Possessive adjectives my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Key pitfall: his/her depends on the owner, not the object (French son/sa). Possessive 's (Marie's car, my parents' house).

lessons.title: A, an et le pluriel
lessons.brief: Articles a/an (an before a vowel SOUND: an hour, a university), regular and irregular plurals (child/children, man/men, person/people, mouse/mice). Jobs need a/an in English (She is a nurse), unlike French.

units.title: Ma journée
units.goal: Parler de tes habitudes et de ta routine.

lessons.title: Le présent simple : affirmations
lessons.brief: Present simple affirmative for routines and facts. Third person -s/-es/-ies (works, watches, studies) and pronunciation of -s endings (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/). Daily routine verbs: get up, take a shower, have breakfast, go to work, get home.

lessons.title: Do / does : questions et négations
lessons.brief: Present simple negatives (don't/doesn't + base verb) and questions (Do you…? Does she…?) with short answers. Pitfall: no -s after does/doesn't (She doesn't work, Does he like…?).

lessons.title: L’heure et les moments de la journée
lessons.brief: Telling the time the North American way (7:15 = seven fifteen, also quarter past seven; 8:30 = eight thirty / half past eight), a.m./p.m., at/in/on with time (at 8, in the morning, on Monday, at night).

lessons.title: Always, often, never : la fréquence
lessons.brief: Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never), their position (before the main verb, after be), How often…?, once/twice a week, every day.

lessons.title: Les loisirs : like + -ing
lessons.brief: Likes and dislikes: like, love, enjoy, hate, don't mind + -ing (I love skating). Hobbies popular in Quebec: hockey, skiing, hiking, cooking, reading, video games. What do you do in your free time?

units.title: Famille et maison
units.goal: Décrire ta famille, ton logement et les gens autour de toi.

lessons.title: La famille
lessons.brief: Family vocabulary (parents, siblings, cousin, in-laws, stepfather…), have/has for possession (I have two brothers), Do you have…?, How many…? Recognise British have got.

lessons.title: There is / there are
lessons.brief: There is / there are, Is there…? Are there…?, some/any basics, rooms and furniture (living room, kitchen, couch, fridge…).

lessons.title: Les prépositions de lieu
lessons.brief: Prepositions of place: in, on, under, next to, between, behind, in front of, above, across from. Where is…? It's on the table.

lessons.title: This, that, these, those
lessons.brief: Demonstratives for near/far and singular/plural, with objects at home and in a store. What's this? Those are my keys.

lessons.title: Décrire une personne
lessons.brief: Describing appearance (tall, short, curly hair, blue eyes, beard) and personality (friendly, shy, funny). What does he look like? vs What is he like? Adjectives come before the noun and never take -s.

units.title: Manger et acheter
units.goal: Commander, faire des achats et parler de nourriture.

lessons.title: Dénombrable ou indénombrable
lessons.brief: Countable vs uncountable nouns with food (an apple, some bread, some rice), a/an/some/any, a piece of / a bottle of / a cup of.

lessons.title: How much, how many et les prix
lessons.brief: How much / how many, a lot of / a few / a little, saying prices in dollars and cents ($4.99 = four ninety-nine), taxes and tips vocabulary.

lessons.title: Au café et au restaurant
lessons.brief: Ordering politely: I'd like…, Can I get…?, Could I have…?, For here or to go?, the check/bill, tipping culture in North America (15–20%). Useful dialogue with a server.

lessons.title: Faire les magasins
lessons.brief: Shopping phrases: Can I try it on?, What size?, It's too big/small, Do you have it in blue?, cash or card, receipt, return/exchange.

lessons.title: Les recettes et l’impératif
lessons.brief: Imperatives (Cut the onions, Don't touch), cooking verbs (boil, fry, mix, bake, chop), sequencing words (first, then, next, finally). Recipe of pancakes with maple syrup.

units.title: Ici et maintenant
units.goal: Décrire ce qui se passe maintenant et te déplacer en ville.

lessons.title: Le présent continu
lessons.brief: Present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) for actions happening now, spelling rules (running, making, lying), present simple vs present continuous basics, stative verbs (like, know, want) not used in -ing.

lessons.title: Les vêtements et la météo
lessons.brief: Clothes (coat, boots, mittens, toque/tuque, scarf) and weather (It's snowing, It's freezing, It's minus twenty, humid, windy). What are you wearing? What's the weather like?

lessons.title: Can et can’t
lessons.brief: Can/can't for ability, possibility and asking permission. Pronunciation: can /kən/ (weak) vs can't /kænt/ (strong). Could for past ability.

lessons.title: Demander son chemin
lessons.brief: Asking for and giving directions: Excuse me, where is…?, go straight, turn left/right, it's on the corner, two blocks away, across from, next to.

lessons.title: Les transports
lessons.brief: Transportation: by bus/car/bike, on foot, take the subway/metro, a ticket, a transfer, How long does it take?, It takes 20 minutes. Commuting vocabulary.

units.title: Hier
units.goal: Raconter ce que tu as fait hier, la semaine passée ou il y a longtemps.

lessons.title: Was et were
lessons.brief: Past of be: was/were, wasn't/weren't, Were you…?, I was born in…, yesterday, last night, last week, … ago.

lessons.title: Le passé simple : verbes réguliers
lessons.brief: Past simple of regular verbs: -ed spelling (stopped, studied, liked) and pronunciation (/t/ worked, /d/ played, /ɪd/ wanted). Time expressions: yesterday, last…, … ago.

lessons.title: Les verbes irréguliers essentiels
lessons.brief: The 25 most common irregular verbs in the past (go/went, have/had, do/did, see/saw, get/got, make/made, come/came, take/took, say/said, buy/bought, eat/ate…) with memory tips.

lessons.title: Questions et négations au passé
lessons.brief: Past simple questions and negatives with did/didn't + base verb (Where did you go? I didn't see it). Pitfall: never didn't went / did you saw.

lessons.title: Raconter sa fin de semaine
lessons.brief: Talking about your weekend: sequencing (first, then, after that), reactions (That sounds fun! Really? Lucky you!), Quebec context (cabane à sucre/sugar shack, chalet/cottage, festival).

levels.name: Élémentaire
levels.desc: Raconter, comparer, parler de projets et te débrouiller dans la vie pratique.

units.title: Raconter une histoire
units.goal: Raconter des événements passés de façon vivante.

lessons.title: Le passé continu
lessons.brief: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) for actions in progress in the past and background descriptions. What were you doing at 8 p.m. last night?

lessons.title: When et while
lessons.brief: Past simple vs past continuous with when and while (I was cooking when the phone rang). Interrupted actions and parallel actions.

lessons.title: Les mots pour raconter
lessons.brief: Narrative linkers: first, then, after that, suddenly, at that moment, finally, in the end, eventually (pitfall: eventually ≠ éventuellement).

lessons.title: Used to : les habitudes passées
lessons.brief: Used to for past habits and states (I used to live in Laval), didn't use to, Did you use to…? Compare with past simple.

lessons.title: Les sentiments : -ed ou -ing ?
lessons.brief: Adjectives ending in -ed vs -ing (bored/boring, interested/interesting, tired/tiring, embarrassed/embarrassing) when telling a memory.

units.title: Comparer
units.goal: Comparer des personnes, des lieux et des objets.

lessons.title: Les comparatifs
lessons.brief: Comparatives: -er / more + adjective + than, spelling (bigger, easier), irregular (good/better, bad/worse, far/farther). Pitfall: more better is wrong.

lessons.title: Les superlatifs
lessons.brief: Superlatives: the -est / the most, irregular (the best, the worst), in/of after superlatives, the best … I've ever…

lessons.title: As… as, too et enough
lessons.brief: (not) as … as for equality, too + adjective, adjective + enough, not enough + noun (It's too cold; I'm not old enough).

lessons.title: Décrire une ville
lessons.brief: City vocabulary (downtown, neighbourhood, suburbs, crowded, quiet, safe) and comparing Montreal, Quebec City, Toronto and Vancouver.

lessons.title: Comparer avant d’acheter
lessons.brief: Comparing products and prices, giving opinions, cheaper/more expensive/better value, reading online reviews, Which one would you recommend?

units.title: L’avenir
units.goal: Parler de tes projets, de tes décisions et faire des prédictions.

lessons.title: Going to : projets et intentions
lessons.brief: Be going to for plans and intentions and for predictions based on evidence (Look at the clouds, it's going to rain). Pronunciation gonna (informal).

lessons.title: Will : décisions, offres et promesses
lessons.brief: Will/won't for instant decisions (I'll have the soup), offers (I'll help you), promises and predictions with I think / probably.

lessons.title: Le présent continu pour l’avenir
lessons.brief: Present continuous for fixed arrangements (I'm meeting Sam tomorrow). Choosing between going to, will and present continuous.

lessons.title: Inviter et répondre
lessons.brief: Invitations and suggestions: Would you like to…?, Do you want to…?, How about…?, Let's…, Why don't we…? Accepting and refusing politely with an excuse.

lessons.title: Préparer un voyage
lessons.brief: Travel planning: booking a flight/hotel, airport vocabulary (check in, boarding pass, gate, carry-on, customs), at the border with US officers.

units.title: Mes expériences
units.goal: Parler de ce que tu as déjà vécu.

lessons.title: Le present perfect : expériences
lessons.brief: Present perfect (have/has + past participle) for life experiences with ever/never. Past participles of common irregular verbs.

lessons.title: Present perfect ou passé simple ?
lessons.brief: Present perfect (unfinished time, no specific time) vs past simple (finished, specific time). Have you ever…? → When did you…? Pitfall: never use present perfect with yesterday/ago/in 2019.

lessons.title: Just, already et yet
lessons.brief: Just, already, yet with the present perfect: meaning and position (I've just arrived; Have you finished yet? I haven't eaten yet).

lessons.title: For et since
lessons.brief: Present perfect with for (duration) and since (starting point) for situations that continue (I've lived here for 5 years / since 2019). Pitfall: French depuis + present → English present perfect.

lessons.title: Been ou gone ?
lessons.brief: Been (went and came back) vs gone (still there). Talking about trips and experiences in a natural conversation.

units.title: Règles et conseils
units.goal: Exprimer des obligations, des interdictions et donner des conseils.

lessons.title: Have to et must
lessons.brief: Obligation with have to and must, absence of obligation don't have to vs prohibition mustn't (big pitfall), had to in the past.

lessons.title: Should : donner des conseils
lessons.brief: Advice with should/shouldn't, ought to, You'd better, Why don't you…? If I were you (recognise).

lessons.title: Chez le médecin
lessons.brief: Body parts and symptoms (I have a headache, a sore throat, a fever, I feel dizzy), at the clinic and the pharmacy, How long have you had it?

lessons.title: Demander poliment
lessons.brief: Polite requests: Can I…?, Could you…?, Would you mind + -ing?, May I…? Answering politely (Sure, Go ahead, I'm afraid not).

lessons.title: Les règles au travail et à l’école
lessons.brief: Rules: be allowed to, not allowed to, can/can't for permission, required, forbidden; signs and notices in English.

units.title: Vie pratique
units.goal: Te débrouiller au téléphone, à l’hôtel et à l’écrit.

lessons.title: Au téléphone
lessons.brief: Phone language: Hello, this is…, Can I speak to…?, Hold on, I'll call you back, Can I leave a message?, spelling names and numbers on the phone.

lessons.title: À l’hôtel
lessons.brief: Hotel vocabulary and problems: check in/out, reservation, The heater doesn't work, Could I get extra towels?, complaining politely.

lessons.title: Les pronoms compléments
lessons.brief: Object pronouns me, you, him, her, it, us, them and their position after the verb (I love it, Call me), after prepositions (with them).

lessons.title: Les adverbes de manière
lessons.brief: Adverbs of manner (quickly, carefully, well, hard, fast, late), adjective vs adverb (He's a good driver / He drives well).

lessons.title: Écrire un courriel simple
lessons.brief: Informal emails: greeting (Hi Sam,), opening lines, thanking, apologising, inviting, closing (Talk soon, Best). Common mistakes of French speakers.

levels.name: Intermédiaire
levels.desc: Te débrouiller dans la plupart des situations, raconter, argumenter et travailler en anglais.

units.title: Le temps qui passe
units.goal: Maîtriser les temps du passé et du present perfect.

lessons.title: Le present perfect continu
lessons.brief: Present perfect continuous (have been + -ing) for duration and recent activities with visible results (You look tired — have you been running?). Simple vs continuous.

lessons.title: Le past perfect
lessons.brief: Past perfect (had + past participle) for the earlier of two past actions, by the time, before, after, already.

lessons.title: Used to, would et be used to
lessons.brief: Used to and would for past habits; be used to / get used to + -ing for familiarity (I'm used to the cold). Big pitfall between them.

lessons.title: Les temps du récit
lessons.brief: Narrative tenses together (past simple, past continuous, past perfect) in a short story.

lessons.title: Raconter une anecdote
lessons.brief: Telling an anecdote: hooks (You won't believe what happened…), reacting (No way! You're kidding! That's hilarious!), keeping the listener interested.

units.title: Si…
units.goal: Exprimer des conditions réelles et imaginaires.

lessons.title: Conditionnels zéro et un
lessons.brief: Zero conditional (facts) and first conditional (real future possibilities), unless, as soon as, when, in case.

lessons.title: Le deuxième conditionnel
lessons.brief: Second conditional for unreal or unlikely present/future situations (If I won the lottery, I would…), If I were you, would/could/might.

lessons.title: Wish et if only au présent
lessons.brief: Wish/if only + past simple for present regrets (I wish I spoke Spanish), wish + could, wish + would for annoyances.

lessons.title: Réel ou imaginaire ?
lessons.brief: Choosing between first and second conditional, giving advice and hypotheses with conditionals.

lessons.title: Débattre d’un sujet de société
lessons.brief: Expressing opinions on social topics (environment, technology, remote work) using conditionals and opinion phrases.

units.title: La voix passive
units.goal: Mettre l’accent sur l’action plutôt que sur la personne.

lessons.title: Le passif : présent et passé
lessons.brief: Passive voice in present and past simple (is made, was built), by + agent, when and why to use the passive.

lessons.title: Le passif aux autres temps
lessons.brief: Passive with present perfect, future, present continuous and modals (has been sold, will be announced, is being repaired, must be done).

lessons.title: Faire faire : have something done
lessons.brief: Causative have/get something done (I had my hair cut, I'm getting my car fixed) for services.

lessons.title: Inventions et faits canadiens
lessons.brief: Passive in context: Canadian inventions and facts (Basketball was invented by a Canadian, insulin was discovered in Toronto).

lessons.title: Lire un texte informatif
lessons.brief: Reading strategies: skimming, scanning, guessing meaning from context, passive voice in news and articles.

units.title: Rapporter des paroles
units.goal: Répéter ce que quelqu’un a dit.

lessons.title: Le discours indirect
lessons.brief: Reported statements with tense backshift (She said she was tired), time/place changes, say vs tell (tell someone).

lessons.title: Rapporter des questions
lessons.brief: Reported questions with if/whether and wh- words, statement word order (She asked me where I lived — not where did I live).

lessons.title: Ordres et demandes
lessons.brief: Reporting orders and requests with tell/ask + object + (not) to + infinitive (He told me to wait).

lessons.title: Les verbes rapporteurs
lessons.brief: Reporting verbs: explain, promise, offer, refuse, remind, warn, agree, + their structures.

lessons.title: Résumer une conversation
lessons.brief: Summarising a conversation or a voicemail for someone else using reported speech.

units.title: Relier les idées
units.goal: Construire des phrases plus longues et mieux liées.

lessons.title: Les propositions relatives
lessons.brief: Defining relative clauses with who, which, that, where, whose, when; omitting the relative pronoun (the book I read).

lessons.title: Gérondif ou infinitif ?
lessons.brief: Verb + -ing (enjoy, avoid, finish, mind) vs verb + to (want, decide, hope, need), verbs that change meaning (stop, remember, try, forget).

lessons.title: Les connecteurs logiques
lessons.brief: Linkers of contrast, cause and purpose: although, however, despite/in spite of, because of, so that, in order to, therefore.

lessons.title: Les verbes à particule courants
lessons.brief: Common phrasal verbs (look for, find out, give up, turn on/off, pick up, run out of, get along with), separable vs inseparable.

lessons.title: Écrire un paragraphe structuré
lessons.brief: Writing a structured paragraph: topic sentence, supporting details, examples, linking words, concluding sentence.

units.title: Au travail
units.goal: Utiliser l’anglais dans un contexte professionnel.

lessons.title: L’entrevue d’embauche
lessons.brief: Job interview: typical questions (Tell me about yourself, strengths and weaknesses, Why do you want this job?) and strong answers.

lessons.title: Le courriel professionnel
lessons.brief: Professional email phrases: I'm writing to…, Please find attached, Could you please…?, I look forward to hearing from you, Best regards.

lessons.title: Les réunions
lessons.brief: Meeting language: agenda, Let's get started, Could I add something?, interrupting politely, Let's move on, action items.

lessons.title: Donner son opinion
lessons.brief: Giving opinions and agreeing/disagreeing politely: In my opinion, I see your point, but…, I partly agree, I'm not so sure.

lessons.title: Parler de son parcours
lessons.brief: Talking about your career and CV: responsibilities, achievements (I managed a team of…), skills, transferable skills.

levels.name: Intermédiaire avancé
levels.desc: Comprendre l’essentiel de textes complexes, argumenter et parler avec aisance.

units.title: Récits et regrets
units.goal: Raconter avec précision et exprimer des regrets.

lessons.title: Les temps narratifs avancés
lessons.brief: All narrative tenses including past perfect continuous (She had been waiting for hours) to tell a story with precise time relations.

lessons.title: Le troisième conditionnel
lessons.brief: Third conditional for unreal past (If I had known, I would have come), contractions and pronunciation (I'd've).

lessons.title: Les conditionnels mixtes
lessons.brief: Mixed conditionals: past condition with present result and present condition with past result.

lessons.title: Regrets : wish et should have
lessons.brief: Wish/if only + past perfect, should have / shouldn't have + past participle for regrets and criticism.

lessons.title: Raconter avec style
lessons.brief: Vivid storytelling: precise verbs (stroll, rush, whisper, grab), adverbs, direct speech, suspense.

units.title: Déduire et supposer
units.goal: Faire des déductions et parler de probabilités.

lessons.title: Must, might, can’t au présent
lessons.brief: Modals of deduction in the present: must (certain), might/may/could (possible), can't (impossible).

lessons.title: Must have, might have, can’t have
lessons.brief: Modals of deduction about the past: must have done, might have done, can't/couldn't have done.

lessons.title: Exprimer la probabilité
lessons.brief: Probability expressions: likely/unlikely, bound to, there's a good chance, probably/definitely position, I doubt it.

lessons.title: Seem, appear et look like
lessons.brief: Seem, appear, look/sound/feel like, as if / as though for impressions.

lessons.title: Résoudre un mystère
lessons.brief: Speculating about a mystery situation using all deduction structures.

units.title: Phrases complexes
units.goal: Écrire et parler avec des structures plus riches.

lessons.title: Les relatives explicatives
lessons.brief: Non-defining relative clauses with commas, which referring to a whole clause, whom, of which.

lessons.title: Les propositions participiales
lessons.brief: Participle clauses: Having finished…, Not knowing what to do…, Built in 1850, the house…

lessons.title: La mise en relief
lessons.brief: Cleft sentences: What I need is…, It was Tom who…, The thing that…, for emphasis.

lessons.title: Éviter les répétitions
lessons.brief: Substitution and ellipsis: so/not (I think so, I hope not), do so, one/ones, auxiliaries in short answers.

lessons.title: Les déterminants avancés
lessons.brief: All/whole/every/each, both/either/neither, none of, any vs every.

units.title: Le passif et le discours avancés
units.goal: Rapporter des informations comme dans les médias.

lessons.title: It is said that…
lessons.brief: Passive reporting structures: It is said/believed/reported that…, He is thought to be…, She is said to have…

lessons.title: Les verbes rapporteurs avancés
lessons.brief: Reporting verbs with patterns: suggest/recommend + -ing or that, deny/admit + -ing, accuse of, apologise for, insist on.

lessons.title: Le causatif avancé
lessons.brief: Causative structures: get someone to do, have someone do, make/let someone do.

lessons.title: Lire la presse
lessons.brief: Newspaper and headline language (headlines grammar, idioms in news), understanding bias.

lessons.title: Rédiger un rapport
lessons.brief: Writing a report: headings, objective tone, recommendations, passive structures.

units.title: Enrichir son vocabulaire
units.goal: Parler de façon plus naturelle et précise.

lessons.title: Les collocations
lessons.brief: Collocations: make vs do, have/take, strong/heavy, adjective + noun pairs that sound natural (heavy traffic, strong coffee).

lessons.title: Les verbes à particule avancés
lessons.brief: Advanced phrasal verbs: come up with, put up with, look forward to, turn down, carry out, figure out, bring up.

lessons.title: Les expressions idiomatiques
lessons.brief: Common idioms in North American English (piece of cake, under the weather, hit the road, cost an arm and a leg, break the ice).

lessons.title: La formation des mots
lessons.brief: Word formation with prefixes and suffixes (un-, dis-, mis-, -ness, -ment, -able, -ful, -less).

lessons.title: Les faux amis
lessons.brief: False friends for French speakers: actually, eventually, library, sensible, assist, deceive, attend, rude, location, pretend, currently.

units.title: Convaincre
units.goal: Argumenter, nuancer et présenter.

lessons.title: Argumenter et débattre
lessons.brief: Presenting arguments, counter-arguments and concessions: Admittedly, On the other hand, Nevertheless, That may be true, but…

lessons.title: Nuancer son propos
lessons.brief: Hedging: It seems that, tend to, arguably, to some extent, it could be argued that, a significant number of.

lessons.title: Registre formel ou familier
lessons.brief: Formal vs informal register and equivalents (get/obtain, ask/inquire, help/assist, need/require).

lessons.title: Faire une présentation
lessons.brief: Presentation language: signposting (First, I'll…, Let's move on to…, To sum up), describing graphs and trends.

lessons.title: La lettre de plainte
lessons.brief: Writing a complaint: structure, polite but firm tone, describing the problem, requesting action.

levels.name: Avancé
levels.desc: T’exprimer avec aisance et précision, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, même dans des contextes exigeants.

units.title: Emphase et style
units.goal: Donner du relief et du style à ton anglais.

lessons.title: L’inversion
lessons.brief: Inversion after negative adverbials: Never have I…, Not only… but also, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly… when, No sooner… than, Only then.

lessons.title: Clivées avancées et fronting
lessons.brief: Advanced cleft sentences (All I want is…, The reason why…, What happened was…) and fronting for emphasis.

lessons.title: L’emphase et les intensifs
lessons.brief: Emphatic do (I do understand), intensifiers (utterly, by far, such/so), emphasis in speech.

lessons.title: La cohésion du discours
lessons.brief: Cohesion: referencing, discourse markers (that said, as a result, on balance, by the same token).

lessons.title: Style et rythme
lessons.brief: Sentence variety, parallelism, concision, avoiding repetition in writing.

units.title: Nuances grammaticales
units.goal: Maîtriser les subtilités de la grammaire.

lessons.title: Futur continu et futur antérieur
lessons.brief: Future continuous and future perfect (will be doing, will have done), be about to, be due to, be on the verge of.

lessons.title: Les modaux avancés
lessons.brief: Advanced modals: needn't have vs didn't need to, would rather, may well, be supposed to, be bound to.

lessons.title: Le subjonctif et les structures formelles
lessons.brief: Subjunctive and formal structures: insist that he be, It's vital that, were to, Should you need anything.

lessons.title: Les prépositions dépendantes
lessons.brief: Dependent prepositions after adjectives, verbs and nouns (responsible for, insist on, in charge of, aware of), French-speaker traps.

lessons.title: Le temps grammatical vs le temps réel
lessons.brief: Past forms for hypothetical meaning (It's time we left, I'd rather you didn't), present for future in time clauses.

units.title: Écrire comme un pro
units.goal: Rédiger des textes clairs, structurés et convaincants.

lessons.title: La nominalisation
lessons.brief: Nominalisation for formal style (decide → the decision to), noun phrases in academic and business writing.

lessons.title: L’essai argumentatif
lessons.brief: Argumentative essay: thesis, topic sentences, evidence, counter-argument, conclusion.

lessons.title: La correspondance formelle
lessons.brief: Advanced formal correspondence: cover letters, proposals, diplomatic refusals.

lessons.title: Réviser son texte
lessons.brief: Editing and proofreading: common errors of French speakers (capitalisation, punctuation, word order, gallicisms).

lessons.title: Résumer et paraphraser
lessons.brief: Summarising and paraphrasing techniques, synonyms, changing structure while keeping meaning.

units.title: Langue idiomatique
units.goal: Comprendre et utiliser l’anglais naturel des natifs.

lessons.title: Les idiomes avancés
lessons.brief: Advanced idioms with body parts and colours (keep an eye on, out of the blue, see red, a green light).

lessons.title: Particules à plusieurs sens
lessons.brief: Phrasal verbs with multiple meanings (take off, pick up, turn out, come across, make out, put off).

lessons.title: Binômes et expressions figées
lessons.brief: Binomials and fixed expressions (safe and sound, pros and cons, sooner or later, by and large).

lessons.title: L’anglais familier nord-américain
lessons.brief: North American informal English and slang (gonna, wanna, y'all, What's up, no worries, my bad, I'm down), when to use it.

lessons.title: Les métaphores du quotidien
lessons.brief: Everyday metaphors: time is money, business is war, ideas are food (food for thought, half-baked).

units.title: Comprendre finement
units.goal: Saisir l’humour, l’implicite et les accents.

lessons.title: L’humour et le sarcasme
lessons.brief: Irony, sarcasm and understatement, recognising tone (Oh, great…), British vs American humour.

lessons.title: Le sens implicite
lessons.brief: Implied meaning and polite indirectness (I'm not sure that's the best idea = no), reading between the lines.

lessons.title: Les accents anglophones
lessons.brief: Differences between US, UK, Canadian and Australian English: vocabulary, spelling (colour/color), pronunciation.

lessons.title: La parole rapide
lessons.brief: Connected speech: reductions (gonna, wanna, gotta, whaddaya), linking, weak forms, elision.

lessons.title: Écouter des contenus authentiques
lessons.brief: Strategies for podcasts, series and news: prediction, note-taking, dealing with unknown words.

units.title: Anglais professionnel
units.goal: Négocier, diriger et convaincre au travail.

lessons.title: Négocier
lessons.brief: Negotiation language: proposals, conditional offers (If you…, we could…), compromise, closing a deal.

lessons.title: Donner de la rétroaction
lessons.brief: Diplomatic feedback: softening criticism, the feedback sandwich, constructive suggestions.

lessons.title: Animer une réunion
lessons.brief: Chairing a meeting: opening, managing turns, keeping on track, summarising decisions.

lessons.title: Persuader par écrit
lessons.brief: Persuasive writing techniques: benefits, social proof, calls to action, tone.

lessons.title: Le small talk professionnel
lessons.brief: Networking and small talk: opening lines, keeping a conversation going, exiting gracefully.

levels.name: Maîtrise
levels.desc: Comprendre pratiquement tout et t’exprimer avec la précision et la finesse d’un locuteur natif instruit.

units.title: Précision
units.goal: Choisir le mot exact et la nuance juste.

lessons.title: Quasi-synonymes et connotations
lessons.brief: Near-synonyms and connotation (thin/slim/skinny, stubborn/determined, cheap/inexpensive, persuade/convince).

lessons.title: Changer de registre
lessons.brief: Rewriting the same message in different registers (casual, neutral, formal, academic).

lessons.title: Les figures de style
lessons.brief: Rhetorical devices: alliteration, hyperbole, litotes, rhetorical questions, the rule of three.

lessons.title: Grammaire de haut niveau
lessons.brief: Very advanced grammar: inverted conditionals (Had I known…), complex noun phrases, advanced ellipsis.

lessons.title: Nuances de modalité
lessons.brief: Subtle modality: may/might/could in hedging, would/should in formal writing, epistemic stance.

units.title: Culture et références
units.goal: Comprendre les références culturelles des anglophones.

lessons.title: Shakespeare et la Bible au quotidien
lessons.brief: Everyday expressions from Shakespeare and the Bible (break the ice, a wild goose chase, the writing on the wall, a good Samaritan).

lessons.title: Les métaphores sportives
lessons.brief: North American sports metaphors (ballpark figure, drop the ball, hat trick, step up to the plate, a slam dunk).

lessons.title: Proverbes et dictons
lessons.brief: Proverbs and sayings, their meaning and how natives allude to them partially (when in Rome…).

lessons.title: L’humour et les jeux de mots
lessons.brief: Puns, wordplay and cultural references in TV and ads.

lessons.title: L’anglais du Canada
lessons.brief: Canadian English and culture: eh, toque, loonie/toonie, washroom, double-double, poutine debates, spelling, politeness.

units.title: Écriture experte
units.goal: Écrire avec l’aisance d’un auteur.

lessons.title: L’essai critique
lessons.brief: Critical essays: evaluating arguments, evidence and assumptions.

lessons.title: La concision
lessons.brief: Eliminating wordiness, redundant phrases, weak verbs and nominal style when it hurts clarity.

lessons.title: L’écriture créative
lessons.brief: Creative writing: show, don't tell, imagery, dialogue punctuation, voice.

lessons.title: La critique et la recension
lessons.brief: Writing reviews of books, films and restaurants with nuanced evaluation.

lessons.title: L’anglais académique
lessons.brief: Academic English: citing sources, hedging, academic vocabulary, formal structures.

units.title: Oral expert
units.goal: Parler avec impact, naturel et précision.

lessons.title: L’art de raconter
lessons.brief: Storytelling for impact: structure, pacing, tension, punchlines.

lessons.title: Répliquer dans un débat
lessons.brief: Rebuttals: conceding, countering, reframing, handling tough questions.

lessons.title: Intonation et accent tonique
lessons.brief: Sentence stress and intonation changing meaning (I didn't say she stole it), intonation for attitude.

lessons.title: Parler en public
lessons.brief: Public speaking: openings, rhetorical techniques, pauses, closing strongly.

lessons.title: L’aisance naturelle
lessons.brief: Sounding natural: fillers (well, you know, I mean), hesitation strategies, backchanneling, rephrasing on the fly.
